ambiguities.text: No input validation or sanitization is documented for the hash functions.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume hash functions accept any valid bytes/bytearray without length limits. The underlying Keccak implementation handles arbitrary-length inputs.

ambiguities.text: Error handling behavior is not specified for edge cases.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume hash functions are pure computations that do not raise exceptions for valid byte inputs. Invalid input types would raise standard Python type errors.

implicit_assumptions.description: The underlying Keccak cryptographic primitive implementation is correct and secure.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Compromised hash function could enable collision attacks, allowing attackers to create transactions or blocks with same hash but different content.

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot find Keccak256 or Keccak512 collisions in practical time.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Hash collision would enable replay attacks, state root forgery, and transaction substitution attacks.

implicit_assumptions.description: The hash computation is deterministic across all Ethereum client implementations.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Non-deterministic hashing would cause consensus failures as nodes compute different hashes for same input.
